title: Mar Zutra the Pious
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman finds no halakhot of his, only his great deeds, as in Moed Katan 17b and Nedarim 7b: when a Torah scholar was liable to a ban, he would first ban himself and then ban him; when he entered his lodging, he would release himself and then release him. In Jerusalem Talmud Maaser Sheni 5:5 they said: “Like Mar Zutra, who would pray for others and be answered, but for himself would not be answered”; Hyman suggests that this is Mar Zutra the Pious. In Bava Kamma 81b, he would take (a pebble from others’ fence) and tell his attendant, “Go and throw it back.”

Bava Metzia 24a relates that once a silver cup was stolen from him. He saw a student who washed his hands and dried them on his fellow’s cloak; he said, “This is the one who stole,” bound him, and he confessed. Hyman suggests that he was Exilarch, as we find in Sanhedrin 7b: “Mar Zutra the Pious, when they carried him on their shoulders on the Shabbat of the festival, would say: For strength is not forever.” Yoma 87a reads Rav Zutra, but Ein Yaakov there reads Mar Zutra the Pious. Hyman suggests that perhaps he is the Mar Zutra mentioned in Seder Olam Zuta: “Mar Zutra died, and Kahana his son succeeded him.” Hyman regards Seder Olam Zuta as so corrupt that it is impossible to know properly in which generation he lived. The book Perushim veHe’arot, p. 58, wishes to say that he is Mar Zutra Rabbah, argues at length and, in Hyman’s judgment, comes up with nothing.

notes.text: The saved full Guggenheimer MaaserSheni5:5 paragraph9 supports מתעני as is answered, not fasts; retain the original note’s parenthetical pebble and כפתיה bound him. Exilarch identity, possible SederOlamZuta equivalence and its chronology are Hyman’s uncertain arguments. RavZutra/MarZutra witness forms remain distinct.

The consulted Maaser Sheni 5:5 passage contrasts benefit to the world with sages’ own lack of benefit and directly says Zutra prays for others and is answered, but is not answered for himself. His exilarch status, proposed Seder Olam Zuta identity, uncertain generation and rejected Zutra Rabbah equation remain Hyman’s arguments.
